doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: Tom brings Yank Johnson and Sonny Handy to his band
summary: Tom says he was first to take Yank across the river to play trombone with Isaiah's band, and also found Sonny Handy, who stayed with him almost four years. He mentions touring by train in Texas.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well I was the first one carrying Yank crossing the Pest Christian.
I carried him over there. Him, his brother Isaiah carried the band over there. Not Yank.
You're talking about Sam. I mean... Well I'm talking about Yank was playing the trombone with him. Oh yeah.

He was playing trombone. I was the first one to take him over there. And Handy, he was playing the Pest. And so every time I'd go in the Morgan City play I'd come here. I had to go over, of course, to play with his father, Sonny Handy's father. Well alright. I played there several times and I said this fellow here is too good to be over at the Pest. And I take him over here at the Pest. You know Sonny Handy was playing sax. Yeah. They call him Captain. Yeah. And I take him over here and he stayed full ten. I had that ready. They stayed up there with me for almost four years. I brought him from the Pest. I was playing with his father in there at Pest Christian. And I brought him over there and so they, after I had to go up, I used to go somewhere in Texas. I used to go in Texas, Baltimore, all around the through there I used to play. I used to, Ruffins, used to carry us on the train.
